description: This Go source file implements an HTTP-based client for managing agent nodes, including retrieving health status, restarting servers, fetching tools, shutting down agents, and obtaining agent status with retry and caching mechanisms.

classes.name: HTTPAgentClient
classes.description: HTTPAgentClient is a client implementation that communicates with agent nodes over HTTP, providing methods for health checks, server management, and status retrieval with caching and retry logic.

classes.name: CachedMCPHealth
classes.description: CachedMCPHealth stores cached MCP health data along with a timestamp for cache expiration management.

methods.name: NewHTTPAgentClient
methods.description: Creates a new instance of HTTPAgentClient with specified storage provider and timeout.

methods.name: GetMCPHealth
methods.description: Retrieves MCP health information from an agent node, utilizing cache for efficiency.

methods.name: RestartMCPServer
methods.description: Restarts a specific MCP server on an agent node.

methods.name: GetMCPTools
methods.description: Fetches the list of tools from a specific MCP server.

methods.name: ShutdownAgent
methods.description: Requests a graceful shutdown of an agent node via HTTP.

methods.name: GetAgentStatus
methods.description: Retrieves detailed status information from an agent node with retry and timeout logic.

methods.name: getCachedHealth
methods.description: Internal method to retrieve cached MCP health data if still valid.

methods.name: cacheHealth
methods.description: Stores MCP health data in cache with current timestamp.

methods.name: invalidateCache
methods.description: Removes cached data for a specific node.

methods.name: InvalidateAllCache
methods.description: Clears all cached MCP health data.

methods.name: GetCacheStats
methods.description: Returns statistics about the current cache entries.

methods.name: CleanupExpiredCache
methods.description: Removes expired cache entries based on TTL.

methods.name: isRetryableError
methods.description: Determines if an error is transient and worth retrying.
